facts.claim: AI21 Human or Not reported over 15 million conversations in about 2 months
facts.quote: Since its launch in mid-April, more than 15 million conversations have been conducted in "Human or Not?"

facts.claim: Human or Not: 68% of players guessed human vs bot correctly, so a third were fooled
facts.quote: 68% of people guessed correctly when asked to determine whether they talked to a fellow human or an AI bot.

facts.claim: Aaronson Oracle mechanic: type random f/d keys, oracle predicts the next key, live rolling accuracy shown
facts.quote: Press the 'f' and 'd' keys randomly. As randomly as you can. I'll try to predict which key you'll press next.

facts.claim: Aaronson reported 70-80% prediction of people trying to type randomly (his own claim, not independently tested)
facts.quote: I challenged people to try this and the program was getting between 70% and 80% prediction rates.

facts.claim: Psych-101 is Apache-2.0 with 10.7M human choices from 60k participants
facts.quote: It comprises trial-by-trial data from 160 psychological experiments and 60,092 participants, making 10,681,650 choices.

facts.claim: Centaur is a human-behavior predictor but 70B and not browser-runnable (Llama 3.1 license, needs 2+ 80GB GPUs)
facts.quote: Llama-3.1-Centaur-70B is a foundation model of cognition model that can predict and simulate human behavior

facts.claim: MovieLens 100K is a small stable sequence-ish benchmark; license not on page, defer to README, redistribution restricted
facts.quote: MovieLens 100K movie ratings. Stable benchmark dataset. 100,000 ratings from 1000 users on 1700 movies.

facts.claim: MovieLens usage terms are per-README, not a stated permissive license
facts.quote: Before using these data sets, please review their README files for the usage licenses and other details.

facts.claim: Simile builds an AI simulation of society from real-human-based agents
facts.quote: At Simile, we have built the first AI simulation of society, populated by agents based on real humans.

facts.claim: Simile has $100M funding led by Index Ventures
facts.quote: We are backed by $100M in funding led by Index Ventures.

facts.claim: Aaru sells behavior simulation positioned as more accurate than surveys; no funding on page
facts.quote: Aaru leverages measurable outcomes and actions to become more accurate than any survey or traditional research.

facts.claim: Artificial Societies sells audience-response simulation to consultancies; 3m+ persona library; no funding on page
facts.quote: What we were able to accomplish with Artificial Societies would simply have been impossible with traditional market research

facts.claim: Joon Park's generative_agents repo, the canonical believable-behavior simulator (22.4k stars, Apache-2.0)
facts.quote: It contains our core simulation module for generative agents—computational agents that simulate believable human behaviors.

facts.claim: Byron Knoll's RPS demo runs an LSTM in the browser to predict your next throw
facts.quote: This rock paper scissors AI uses LSTM to predict your next move.

facts.claim: A 2019 JS-only RPS next-move predictor already exists on dev.to (prior art, 2019)
facts.quote: It works by storing your last moves and trying to predict your next ones. The experiment is in JavaScript

facts.claim: Meta HSTU is open-source sequential next-action recommender (2.0k stars, Apache-2.0)
facts.quote: propose efficient algorithms such as HSTU and M-FALCON to accelerate training and inference for large-scale sequential models

facts.claim: Akinator mechanic: guesses what the player is thinking of (launched Aug 2007 per infobox)
facts.quote: it attempts to determine what media or real-life character, object, or animal the player is thinking of
